heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro — production-grade models for premium image and video creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed brand-orange hero with a dark overlay and layered, floating preview cards instead of a split-screen layout. Keep the composition asymmetrical and premium: headline and CTAs anchored left, while the right side is built from stacked image/video sample shells, prompt chips, and a thin marquee of trusted logos. Add subtle grid lines and soft gradient orbs for depth. The treatment should feel warm, high-contrast, and production-ready, with the accent CTA in Techjockey orange and no blue UI cues.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a full-bleed orange hero, then immediately switch to a dark marquee trust band
Use a gallery-led how-it-works section instead of a standard step list
Make Seedream a light, modular spotlight-grid and Seedance a dark cinematic split-panel to avoid repeated layouts
Alternate between dense comparison content and airy proof/testimonial rhythm
Use a centered pricing card after visually rich sections to reset attention before the final CTA
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 & Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore a fast 3-step workflow, industry logos, premium capabilities, pricing, and request a demo.

mustHaveMoments: Prominent logo strip or enterprise trust bar near the top
Text-first hero with concise product positioning and one primary CTA
Lead capture or demo-request block immediately after the hero
Dedicated visual gallery section featuring both images and videos
Separate product detail sections for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro
Pricing or quote blocks framed as consultative next steps
Testimonial section with role-based credibility from creative and marketing professionals
avoidPatterns: Large decorative or overly cinematic hero that delays the value proposition
Secondary CTA clutter or competing conversion paths
Feature dumping without clear separation between image and video capabilities
Badge-only trust treatment without visible logos
Overly airy spacing that reduces the amount of proof and product detail above the fold
Consumer-style promotional language that undermines enterprise credibility
designStrategy.reasoning: This page should prioritize lead generation because the content and pricing imply a consultative purchase flow, not instant self-serve buying. The audience is professional and likely solution-aware, so the page should quickly establish capability, credibility, and a clear next step. Since the instruction says visitors trust logos most, the trust system should be logo-led rather than testimonial-led or stats-led, with badges used only as supporting proof. The structure should follow the reference pattern of a text-first conversion page, but adapted with a gallery section to showcase both image and video outputs. A split hero works best: messaging on one side, visual proof or trust signals on the other, while keeping the dominant emphasis on the product message and conversion action rather than immersive media.

sections.backgroundTreatment: full-bleed orange field with precision-line overlays, floating output frames, prompt chips, and subtle layered motion shells
sections.designNote: Hero must feel dynamic above the fold and answer the quality check: headline states what it is, subheadline states who it is for, CTA is clearly 'Get started'. Use a product-forward visual collage with abstract image/video previews rather than a literal dashboard. Keep copy concise and premium.

Place trust immediately after the hero because traffic is warm and trustStrategy is logos-first. Show 3-6 recognisable SVG logos in a high-contrast marquee band. If logo set is unavailable, fall back to a metric strip, but primary treatment remains logo-led.

Warm traffic sequence requires this section early. Present exactly 3 steps: prompt or upload, generate image/video, refine and export. Keep it fast, confidence-building, and visually expressive with a slim preview rail or mini storyboard. Avoid generic SaaS framing.

Reinforce industry-specific credibility with a secondary proof band using recognisable logos and short use-case labels. Make this section quieter than the first trust band but still prominent. Use strong spacing and no dense copy.

This is one of the two required visually expressive sections. Show mixed image and video previews, prompt-to-result comparisons, and creative outcomes. Use a dark cinematic canvas to contrast with the light process section. Allow the user to browse outcomes by use case instead of reading long paragraphs.

Because there are multiple product sections, alternate layouts. Lead with Seedream 4.5 in a light spotlight-plus-grid treatment with 5 features collapsed into a spotlight and supporting grid. Focus on the click-driving features: advanced text-image alignment, high-resolution output, typographic rendering, multi-image composition, and structural fidelity. Keep the CTA as 'Get started'.

Second product block must feel materially different from the first. Use a dark split-panel list with a preview strip for audio-visual generation. Highlight text-to-video, synchronized audio and video, multilingual lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and 10x faster inference. This section should feel more immersive and motion-led.

Convert interest into action with a centered pricing/comparison treatment. Keep the two plans visually separated but compact, with the Seedance plan receiving a slight emphasis due to published starting price. All buttons must read 'Get started' and remain solid accent orange at full opacity.

With 5 testimonials, use a carousel rather than a static grid. Keep it elegant and low-friction, featuring creative director, video producer, art director, marketing manager, and creative lead voices. Make the carousel feel editorial but not like a generic SaaS quote wall.

Final CTA section should be highly conversion-led and visually isolated. Use a floating centered card on a dark background with one clear action: Get started. Keep mobile CTA full-width. This is the strongest close after proof, pricing, and testimonials.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium enterprise AI with a warm brand-led identity: confident, high-contrast, polished, and production-focused. The page should feel intelligent and trustworthy, with strong logo proof, gallery-driven discovery, layered cards, and a refined orange-on-charcoal visual language that communicates creative power at scale.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium gallery section with mixed video thumbnails and image previews, showing cinematic samples, prompt-to-output comparisons, and multi-panel AI mockups. The hero should feature abstract layered visual shells rather than a literal product screenshot: floating preview cards, timeline strips, prompt chips, and output frames with subtle motion cues. Logos should appear as SVG marquee bands and proof bars to establish trust first. Add a contrast-heavy dark showcase for Seedance 1.5 Pro, with small animated-style preview cards implying synchronized audio-visual generation.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so a smaller hero size is needed to preserve balance and prevent awkward wrapping while still feeling premium.

colours.colourReason: The brand is anchored by Techjockey orange, with white and charcoal as supporting neutrals. Since brandColors.primary is set, the hero background and primary CTA must use that orange. The overall system stays rooted in the brand’s exact colors, with no borrowed palette or gradient default.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen top hero with brand mark above a bold centered headline, a short supporting paragraph, and a compact vertical value-prop list. Visual emphasis is on immediate product positioning rather than a large media-led hero. Best reused as a text-first hero for enterprise/technical products.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero first, then a strong lead-generation form block, followed by product detail sections. The page uses a linear conversion flow with minimal distraction and little sectional complexity.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-first content blocks with simple borders and no decorative card treatment. If cards are used, they should feel functional, dense, and form-adjacent rather than promotional.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears in the hero and again within product sections as conversion-oriented requests/demos. CTA language is action-led and low-friction. Secondary CTA is not emphasized in the reference.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern present; conversion is routed through lead capture and demo/request actions instead of package comparison.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the provided reference, so no reusable footer pattern can be inferred.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible area; the layout is predominantly text and form driven. Suitable for replacing imagery with logos, diagrams, or product UI only if needed, but the reference itself relies on typography and structure.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Sequential product modules with a label, headline, explanatory body copy, and a list of key capabilities. Each module reads as a feature overview section rather than an interactive tabbed experience. Good fit for long-form B2B feature storytelling.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form placed directly below the hero in a prominent content block. Form should feel embedded in the page flow, visually contained, and immediately accessible without modal interaction.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation system is evident in the visible markup; interaction should be static and trust-oriented unless extending the pattern with subtle, non-essential motion.
designNotes: Prioritize clarity, credibility, and fast conversion over visual novelty.
Use one primary action path throughout the page.
Keep hierarchy strong with headline, supporting copy, then benefits.
Maintain a restrained, business-facing layout suitable for technical buyers.
If adapting this pattern, preserve the linear information flow and avoid adding unnecessary interactive complexity.
